verified_metadata.venue: Proceedings of the 35th International Conference on Machine Learning

metadata_sources.supports: Official PMLR record supplies all authors, ICML 2018, volume 80, pp. 5824–5832 and complete BibTeX.

artifact.version_note: Official PMLR proceedings PDF; title and ordered authors match.

contexts.evidence: Section 4 and Theorem 5.4 (pp. 5–6) require integer weights for ordinary tropical rational functions. Proposition 5.6 (p. 7) gives tropical rational signomials for arbitrary real weights. The unqualified wording obscures that distinction.
contexts.proposed_replacement: The geometric reading rests on the identification of \ac{relu} networks with \ac{cpwl} maps and their tropical representations \parencite{Arora2018,Zhang2018,BalestrieroBaraniuk2018MadMax,Misiakos2022,phuong2020functional,Hertrich2023,huchette2025deeplearningmeetspolyhedral}.

contexts.evidence: Proposition 5.1 (p. 6) gives the recursive positive/negative-weight decomposition and max(H,G+t)−G. At ReLU threshold zero this contains max(a,b)−b; Proposition 5.6 extends the construction to real weights.

notes: The paper carefully distinguishes ordinary tropical rational functions (integer network weights) from tropical rational signomials (arbitrary real weights).

contexts.evidence: Sections I.B and III, especially Definition 2 and Theorem 2 (preprint p. 3), develop networks formed as a difference of two convex log-sum-exp functions and establish uniform approximation on compact convex sets. Section VI exploits that DC structure for optimization. This supports the paragraph’s reference to convex network calculus. The paper studies fitting and optimization, rather than attribution or stabilization of an exact split of a pretrained ReLU network.

notes: The key contains 2019, but the existing BibTeX journal year 2020 is correct.
